title: Chalukya Dynasty
capsule: The Chalukyas of Vatapi (Badami Chalukyas) were a Hindu dynasty of the Deccan Plateau in peninsular India, rising to prominence under Pulakesi I who founded Vatapi (modern Badami, Karnataka) as his capital c. 543 AD. The dynasty reached its apex under Pulakesi II (r. 609–642), who repulsed the northward expansion of Emperor Harsha of Kanauj — reportedly near the Narmada River c. 618–619 — and conquered the Vengi delta and much of southern India as far as the Pallava heartland. The Pallavas retaliated: Narasimhavarman I sacked Vatapi in 642, killing Pulakesi II. A dynastic revival under Vikramaditya I recovered Vatapi by 655, but continuing Rashtrakuta pressure culminated in Dantidurga's overthrow of the Chalukya ruler Kirtivarman II around 753–756 AD, ending the Vatapi line.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Badami Chalukya territorial core is well attested by a substantial corpus of copper-plate grants and rock inscriptions; the outer limits of their claimed dominion — especially during Pulakesi II's northern campaigns — are known from boastful prasasti inscriptions and require cautious interpretation.
